ideas.name: Pet Waste Removal

red_team.name: FLOW Edge
attacks: They already use the rink pro shop and trust it with $300 skates.
Pro shops own the rink; most sharpeners are adults behind a counter, not a delivery service.
Yes — a pro shop could add pickup. Defense: subscription relationships with team managers and better turnaround.
One rink with ~300 youth skaters is enough for a teen business; scaling needs more rinks.
$8–12 per sharpen is market rate; a $35/month family plan is plausible for frequent skaters.
Yes with a consumer-grade automatic sharpener (parent purchase) and practice on own skates first.
Rink may forbid on-site commerce — operate via doorstep pickup/drop or get written permission. Liability waiver; parent as business owner on paperwork.
That families will hand skates to a teen. Mitigation: free first sharpen, references from team manager.
red_team.fix: Sell to team managers as a team plan (one pickup, 15 pairs), not to individual parents. Add summer string-run variant to cover seasonality.

red_team.name: Calc Library
attacks: Students lack calculators AND the school doesn't lend. Must verify at your school first.
Easily, but low incentive for others.
red_team.fix: Deposit + rental bundle; partner with math department for referrals; sell refurbished units at semester end.

red_team.name: String Run
attacks: Depends on local courts; pickleball paddles don't need stringing.
Stringing skill takes weeks to learn.
red_team.fix: Fold into FLOW Edge as the warm-season service line rather than a standalone business.
